escalation_reason: Torn between question and bug: the uv build backend docs state that the sdist includes pyproject.toml.orig by design when pyproject.toml is rewritten to TOML 1.0-compatible syntax, so the .orig file is documented behaviour. Whether the rewrite was warranted for this file (the reporter says the author line is valid TOML 1.0) depends on uv's TOML 1.1 detection, which only a maintainer can judge against the full file.
rationale: The reporter's template says bug, but the uv build backend docs (docs/concepts/build-backend.md) explicitly say that when building an sdist the rewritten pyproject.toml is included with the original kept as pyproject.toml.orig, so the .orig file is intended behaviour. The reporter's main claim is that the author line is valid TOML 1.0 and uv nevertheless treats the file as TOML 1.1; the excerpt shows only that line, so whatever construct triggered the rewrite cannot be checked. The author key is also not the PEP 621 field name (authors), which may be a config issue, though I did not verify uv's handling of unknown keys. search_issues found #18055 (a leftover pyproject.toml.orig from a manual patch), which is a different cause and not a duplicate. Classified as question with escalation, because if uv misdetects valid TOML 1.0 as 1.1 this would become a bug.
